risks: Minimal: routine data and a change the clinic is making anyway. The risk is to patients who cannot use the app, handled by keeping paper.
consent: No individual consent for routine data under the service evaluation classification; app users accept the digital health service's terms separately.
data: Pseudonymised extracts; the app export gives completeness by patient study number only (DHS-2026-44).
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: older patients, people with sight problems, people without smartphones and people needing interpreters are least able to use an app; paper stays available, and usable diaries are reported by age and diary type.
effectiveness: Shows whether the switch saves clinic time and what it does to the preventive budget.
efficiency: Existing data; four nurse hours a week.
partnerships: Clinic nurses, the clinic manager, the regional digital health service, the medicines management team and two patient partners with migraine.
rebPath: Service evaluation (SE-NEU-2026-15); no research ethics review required.
limitations: Before-after design; six months after the switch may not reach steady state.
summary: Minimal-risk evaluation with a paper option kept for patients who cannot use the app.
